headlines.title: Coroner says baby with measles in Pennsylvania died of a ruptured spleen
headlines.description: After the Pennsylvania Health Department announced that an infant’s death was associated with measles, the coroner involved has said he does not consider measles to be the cause of death.

headlines.title: Teen Learns to Walk Again After Accident, Now Running Track
headlines.description: After a life-threatening sledding accident at age 6 that left him with a traumatic brain injury, Bensten Schone faced a long and grueling road to recovery. But he refused to let it define his life, learning to breathe, walk and talk again. The now-high school senior is defying the odds by running track. “I love a comeback story, and when they said they didn’t think I could walk again, I was determined to walk and maybe run,” Bensten said. TODAY's Craig Melvin shares his story.

headlines.title: Craving Unhealthy Food? This is What Your Body Really Wants
headlines.description: Food cravings can indicate different things about your health, so TODAY nutrition and health expert Joy Bauer stops by Studio 1A to share the difference between hunger and cravings, how to curb urges, what to reach for instead, the role of GLP-1s, and more.

headlines.title: Patient battles insurance over coverage for tumor removal
headlines.description: Patient battles insurance over coverage for tumor removal In our series “The Cost of Denial,” NBC News’ Anne Thompson reports on short-term insurance plans, which, unlike most other health plans, are not required to cover pre-existing conditions. If you have a story to share, email us at costofdenial@nbcuni.com

headlines.title: Psychiatrist Shares Strategies for Difficult Decision Making
headlines.description: Board-certified psychiatrist Dr. Sue Varma stops by TODAY to share some helpful strategies for decision making, tips to process mixed emotions and the difference between “maximizers” and “good enough” deciders.
